producer_report.summary:
I fixed the starvation: `athena drain` now orders approved steward proposals in the plan like any other item, instead of working them first.

**Root cause.** Drain approved each in-limit proposal before planning. The job it made had no plan entry. Items with no plan entry are batched ahead of every planned item, so the old proposal's job took the job slots from the urgent requests.

**Changes**
- **`crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs`:**
  - **Plan entries.** After approval, `drain_with` asks `steps.plan_entry` for each new job and adds it to the plan. The plan's entries are then sorted back into age order, which is the tiebreak.
  - **Priority.** `RealSteps::entry_of` now finds the proposal behind an approved job and sets its priority through `proposal_priority`. A new `role_priority` helper reads a `Priority: <level>` line from the raising role's newest prompt.
  - **Docs.** The module docs describe the new behaviour. If a job has no plan entry, drain adds a note.
- **`crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs`:** New `proposal_priority(record, own, role)`:
  - A priority record decides alone.
  - Otherwise the job's own non-normal priority (its words or reading) stands.
  - Otherwise the role's default applies, which is normal if the role states none.
  - The module docs mention it.
- **Tests:**
  - **`plan.rs`:** Two new unit tests cover ordering by dependency, priority, rung and age, and the priority rules.
  - **`tests/drain.rs`:** Four new tests:
    - With one job slot, an in-limit proposal and an urgent queued request, drain works the urgent request and leaves the proposal's job queued. With room for both, the urgent request runs first.
    - A proposal whose job is urgent goes first, and the job limit still holds.
    - A proposal is not approved when there is no job-limit room.
    - A real-steps test checks that `drain::plan` lists the approved job in its ordered place, with normal priority by default, high from a role `Priority: high` line, and low from a priority record that beats the role.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`:** A new `### Fixed` entry under Unreleased.

**Checks.** I ran the drain, plan and policy tests, fmt `--check` and clippy with `-D warnings`; all pass. I did not run the full `cargo test` suite. I did not revert the fix to run the new drain test on the old code, so "fails on the old behaviour" rests on reading the old code.

There is one gap against the request, listed in the open issues: `athena plan` lists approved jobs in place, but not open in-limit proposals that no one has approved yet.

criteria_check.criterion: A new drain test (run with cargo test -p athena-cli drain) with an approved in-limit proposal and an urgent queued request works the urgent request first, and fails on the old behavior.
criteria_check.evidence: New test an_urgent_queued_request_is_worked_before_an_approved_in_limit_proposal in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, passes under `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`. With one job slot only `run urgent` happens and the proposal's job stays queued; with room for both, urgent runs first. On the old code the approved job had no plan entry and was placed ahead of every planned item, so `run job-of-...` came first and the test would fail. I did not revert the fix to run it, so the failure on the old code is from reading the old code, not from a run.

criteria_check.criterion: A test shows the plan (Plan::build / the plan command path) lists an approved proposal at its ordered place by dependency, priority, rung, then age, defaulting to normal priority, with role or priority-record overrides honored.
criteria_check.evidence: plan.rs tests an_approved_proposal_is_ordered_among_other_items_by_dependency_priority_rung_then_age and an_approved_proposal_is_normal_unless_a_record_or_its_role_says_otherwise (both pass). The real path is covered by tests/drain.rs the_plan_lists_an_approved_proposal_in_its_ordered_place_with_priority_from_the_record_or_its_role: real RealSteps and drain::plan put the urgent request first and the older approved job before the normal request. The entry's priority is normal by default, high after a role prompt `Priority: high`, and low after a priority record, which wins over the role.

criteria_check.criterion: Drain no longer works approved proposals ahead of the plan; approved proposals are ordered by the same rules as other items and job-limit/budget handling still applies.
criteria_check.evidence: In drain.rs drain_with, each job approved in this pass gets its plan entry via steps.plan_entry and joins view.plan, so Plan::build orders it. RealSteps::entry_of applies proposal_priority (record, then the job's own words, then the role's default). Approval is still gated by approve_all on job-limit and budget room. Tests: the one-slot test stops at JobLimit, a_proposal_that_fits_neither_the_job_limit_nor_the_budget_is_not_approved_even_with_a_plan passes, and the existing an_approval_that_does_not_fit_the_budget test still passes.

open_issues: `athena plan` does not list in-limit proposals that are still open and not yet approved. plan() approves nothing and calls no model. It lists approved jobs (made by `athena approve-work` or by an earlier drain) in their ordered place. A drain approves open in-limit proposals, then orders them. Showing unapproved ones in `athena plan` would need a pre-approval PlanEntry with no acceptance. The brief's design allows approval to stay in drain, so I did not add it.

Approval still happens up front for in-limit proposals, in age order, within the job-limit and budget room. A later drain with more room can approve proposals this one left open. The approval's reading cost is spent even if the job's turn in the plan is not reached; the job stays approved and queued for the next drain.
If a Steps implementation returns no plan entry for an approved job, the job still keeps its old place ahead of the plan and drain adds a note. The real steps always return an entry.
mistakes: My first proposal_priority took the more urgent of the job's own priority and the role's, so an explicit `Priority: low` on the job lost to a role default. A plan.rs test caught it. I changed it so a non-normal own priority beats the role, and the role's default applies only when the job's words say nothing.
learnings: Root cause: drain approved in-limit proposals before planning, and the resulting jobs had no PlanEntry in QueueView.plan. Items with no plan entry are batched ahead of every planned item, so they jumped the queue and took the job slots.

Priority records can only be set on Queued jobs (Athena::set_priority). A job made by approve_work is already read and Proposed, so a record on a proposal's job has to be written directly, as my test does.
Roles have no priority field in RoleDefinition (deny_unknown_fields); the role default is read from a `Priority: <level>` line in the newest version's prompt.
Priority ordering: Urgent < High < Normal < Low, and Plan::build sorts the best first.
Drain tests live in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs; the in-file tests in drain.rs are few.
desires: A way to run the new test against the base commit's code to show it fails there (Bash allows only cargo and git read commands, so I could not revert and rerun).
A RoleDefinition field for default priority; I used a `Priority:` line in the role prompt to avoid a record schema change.
